sections.title: Definitions

summary.text: Defines the key terms used in the TB screening guidelines, including active, enhanced and passive case-finding, computer-aided detection, number needed to screen and repeat screening. It also explains initial screening, triage and the meaning of TB disease as distinct from TB infection.

sections.extract: Definitions The definitions below apply to terms as used in these guidelines, and they may have different meanings elsewhere. Active (tuberculosis) case-finding (ACF): Provider-initiated screening and testing in communities by mobile teams, often using mobile X-ray and rapid molecular tests. The term is sometimes used synonymously with “systematic screening”. Computer-aided detection (CAD): The use of specialized

sections.title: Executive summary

summary.text: Summarizes why WHO updated its 2013 guidance on systematic TB screening, citing the 2.9 million people with TB who went undiagnosed or unreported in 2019 and global targets for diagnosis. It explains that a Guideline Development Group reviewed new evidence in 2020, including on computer-aided detection of chest X-rays, C-reactive protein and rapid molecular tests. The summary presents the recommendations on which populations to screen and which tools to use, ending with a box on the main changes from the earlier guidance.

sections.extract: Executive summary Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, despite being largely curable and preventable. In 2019 an estimated 2.9 million of the 10 million people who fell ill with TB were not diagnosed or reported to the World Health Organization (WHO). sections.title: Background

summary.text: Gives the background to the update, noting the gap in TB diagnosis, the End TB Strategy and UN targets, and the new evidence on screening since WHO's 2013 guidelines.

sections.extract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, despite being largely curable and preventable. In 2019, an estimated 2.9 million of the 10 million people who fell ill with TB were not diagnosed or reported to the World Health Organization (WHO) (1). WHO’s End TB Strategy envisions a 90% reduction in TB incidence and a 95% reduction in TB deaths by 2035 (2, 3), and the Declaration

sections.title: Definition and objectives of systematic screening for TB disease

summary.text: Defines systematic screening for TB disease as provider-initiated identification of people at risk in a target group using rapid tests, followed by diagnostic confirmation. It sets out the two aims of screening: early detection and treatment for individuals, and reduced transmission and incidence in the population.

sections.extract: for TB disease For the purpose of this guideline, systematic screening for TB disease is defined as the systematic identification of people at risk for TB disease, in a predetermined target group, by assessing symptoms and using tests, examinations or other procedures that can be applied rapidly. sections.title: Scope of the 2021 update

summary.text: Presents the conceptual framework for the 2021 update, linking screening inputs and activities to individual and population outcomes such as earlier diagnosis, better treatment results and reduced transmission. It then lists the PICO and background questions used to gather evidence, covering effectiveness, screening tool accuracy, numbers needed to screen, risk factors, costs and community attitudes.

sections.extract: Fig. 1 summarizes the potential contribution of TB screening to standard TB care practices based on the above frameworks for TB screening and shows the conceptual framework that guided the 2021 update to the TB screening guidelines. sections.title: Rationale for the guideline update

summary.text: Explains that the update was prompted by many new studies on screening impact and by prevalence surveys showing a larger TB burden than previously thought.

sections.extract: Since the publication of the first WHO guidelines on systematic screening for TB in 2013 (5), there have been numerous studies, including reviews, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, modelling and cost–effectiveness research, evaluating the real or potential impacts of screening interventions on both individual-level and community-level outcomes related to TB. There have also been numerous

sections.title: Objectives of guideline update

summary.text: States the objectives of the update: to help countries implement effective screening with current evidence on impact, yield and tool performance, and to find more people with TB earlier.

sections.extract: The specific objectives of the guideline update are: 1. to support Member States in implementing effective TB screening interventions by providing updated information about the expected impact of TB screening on patient-important outcomes and the epidemiology of TB, the expected yield of screening interventions and the expected performance of different screening tools and algorithms; 2. to contribute to finding more

sections.title: Target audience

summary.text: Identifies the intended readers of the guideline, such as national TB and HIV programme staff, policymakers and clinicians, and points to an accompanying operational handbook for adapting the recommendations locally.

sections.extract: This guideline is intended for personnel working in national TB programmes, national HIV/AIDS programmes or their equivalents, and other relevant national health programmes in ministries of health; other relevant ministries working in public health and screening; and for other health policymakers, clinicians and public health practitioners working on TB, HIV and infectious diseases in the public and private sectors.

sections.title: Recommendations for systematic screening for TB disease in targeted populations

summary.text: Introduces the population-specific recommendations, explaining that screening may cover whole communities or be targeted at higher-risk groups and how strong and conditional recommendations are distinguished. It sets out the recommendation on screening the general population in high-prevalence settings. The evidence reviewed includes trials and studies in which community-wide screening reduced TB prevalence or infection among children.

sections.extract: systematic screening for TB disease in targeted populations In this guideline, recommendations about systematic screening for TB disease are made for distinct populations for whom it is judged that the benefits and desirable effects of screening outweigh the potential harms. Systematic screening for TB disease can be done for an entire population (community-wide screening) or it can be targeted at selected risk

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease in the general population

summary.text: Explains why the prevalence threshold for general population screening was lowered from 1% to 0.5% undetected TB, and discusses implementation factors such as prevalence, coverage and the sensitivity of screening algorithms. It also covers possible harms and concerns of people being screened, such as stigma and confidentiality.

sections.extract: population was recommended in defined populations with extremely high levels of undetected TB, defined as a 1% prevalence or higher. Based on the updated evidence reviewed, the GDG concluded that the threshold of 1% recommended in the 2013 guidelines could be lowered, but considered that screening under programmatic conditions would not perform as well as was observed in the trial in Viet Nam and, therefore,

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease among people with structural risk factors for TB

summary.text: Gives the conditional recommendation to screen groups with structural risk factors, such as urban poor, homeless, remote, indigenous, migrant and displaced populations, and explains these risk factors. It notes that no new evidence was found since 2013 and offers implementation advice, including combining TB screening with other health activities.

sections.extract: people with structural risk factors for TB 2. Systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted among subpopulations with structural risk factors for TB. These include urban poor communities, homeless communities, communities in remote or isolated areas, indigenous populations, migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons and other vulnerable or marginalized groups with limited access to health care (existing

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease among people living with HIV

summary.text: Sets out the strong recommendation that people living with HIV be screened for TB at every health facility visit, citing their much higher TB risk, and describes follow-up diagnostic testing and preventive treatment.

sections.extract: people living with HIV 3. People living with HIV should be systematically screened for TB disease at each visit to a health facility (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 2.3.1 Summary of evidence and rationale People living with HIV are approximately 19 times more likely to develop TB disease than those without HIV; in 2019, an estimated 44% of people living with HIV who

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease among household and other close contacts of individuals with TB disease

summary.text: Gives the updated strong recommendation to screen household and close contacts of people with TB, citing a pooled disease prevalence of 3.6% and trials in Viet Nam, South Africa and Zambia showing benefits. It then covers implementation, including prioritizing contacts and offering HIV testing and preventive treatment where appropriate.

sections.extract: household and other close contacts of individuals with TB disease 4. Household contacts and other close contacts of individuals with TB disease should be systematically screened for TB disease (updated recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence). 2.4.1 Summary of evidence and rationale Household and close contacts of individuals with TB disease are at high risk of TB infection and

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease in prisons and other penitentiary institutions

summary.text: Presents the updated strong recommendation for TB screening in prisons, citing a much higher TB incidence among prisoners and studies showing earlier and increased case detection. Implementation advice covers screening at entry and periodically, infection control and access to diagnosis.

sections.extract: and other penitentiary institutions 5. Systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted in prisons and penitentiary institutions (updated recommendation: strong recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 2.5.1 Summary of evidence and rationale People in prisons and other penitentiary institutions are at an increased risk for TB compared with the general population, and they often have limited access to

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease among miners and others exposed to silica dust

summary.text: Sets out the strong recommendation to screen current and former workers exposed to silica dust, given the high TB risk linked to silicosis, and advises screening at least every 12 months, ideally combined with improvements to working conditions.

sections.extract: miners and others exposed to silica dust 6. Current and former workers in workplaces with silica exposure should be systematically screened for TB disease (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 2.6.1 Summary of evidence and rationale Exposure to silica dust and silicosis are among the strongest risk factors for TB, with a relative risk of 2.8–39 for silicosis, depending on the

sections.title: Systematic screening for TB disease among people attending health care services who have clinical risk factors for TB

summary.text: Gives conditional recommendations to screen people with clinical TB risk factors in health care settings where prevalence is at least 100 per 100,000, and people with untreated fibrotic lesions on chest X-ray. It reviews evidence on risk factors such as HIV, diabetes, malnutrition, smoking and alcohol use, summarized in a table. Implementation points include prioritizing groups according to local epidemiology, offering preventive treatment where appropriate and considering screening of health care workers.

sections.extract: people attending health care services who have clinical risk factors for TB 7. In settings where the TB prevalence in the general population is 100/100 000 population or higher, systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted among people with a risk factor for TB who are either seeking health care or who are already in care (existing recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

sections.title: Recommendations for tools for systematic screening for TB disease

summary.text: Introduces the recommendations on screening tools, explaining that tools separate people likely to have TB from those unlikely to have it and must be followed by diagnostic tests, and cites WHO target accuracy benchmarks.

sections.extract: for systematic screening for TB disease TB screening tools are designed to distinguish people with a higher probability of having TB disease from those with a low probability and can be assumed to be free of TB disease. They are not intended to provide a definitive diagnosis. In general, they need to be able to be implemented easily and relay results rapidly in order to be informative in a screening context.

sections.title: Tools for screening for TB disease among the general population and high-risk groups

summary.text: Recommends that people aged 15 and over in groups eligible for screening may be screened with symptom questions, chest X-ray or rapid molecular tests, alone or combined. It summarizes systematic review evidence on the accuracy of each tool, with a table of sensitivity and specificity. The section closes by advising countries to fit these tools into national algorithms according to goals, resources and equity.

sections.extract: general population and high-risk groups 9. Among individuals aged 15 years and older in populations in which TB screening is recommended, systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted using a symptom screen, chest X-ray or molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests, alone or in combination (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy). 3.1.1 Summary

sections.title: Use of computer-aided detection software for automated reading of digital chest radiographs

summary.text: Presents a new conditional recommendation that computer-aided detection software may replace human readers in interpreting digital chest X-rays for TB screening and triage in people aged 15 and over. It explains that chest radiography is limited by shortages of trained readers and variability between readers, and that many software packages now estimate the likelihood of TB. It ends with implementation needs such as digital radiography equipment, stable internet and maintenance, noting that costs depend on the setting.

sections.extract: automated reading of digital chest radiographs 10. Among individuals aged 15 years and older in populations in which TB screening is recommended, computer-aided detection software programmes may be used in place of human readers for interpreting digital chest X-rays for screening and triage for TB disease (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 3.2.1 Summary of the evidence and

sections.title: Tools for screening for TB disease among people living with HIV

summary.text: Sets out recommendations on tools for TB screening among adults and adolescents living with HIV, keeping the four-symptom screen and adding C-reactive protein above 5 mg/L, chest X-ray and molecular rapid tests as options. It also strongly recommends systematic molecular testing of HIV inpatients in medical wards where TB prevalence exceeds 10%. The section summarises the evidence on the accuracy of these tools, as the start and end of this cut block show. It ends by encouraging countries to monitor screening yield among people with HIV by screening tool.

sections.extract: living with HIV 11. Among adults and adolescents living with HIV, systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted using the WHO-recommended four symptom screen and those who report any one of the symptoms of current cough, fever, weight loss or night sweats may have TB and should be evaluated for TB and other diseases (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence). 12. sections.title: Tools for systematic screening for TB disease among children and adolescents

summary.text: Gives recommendations for screening children and adolescents, using symptoms, chest radiography or both for close contacts under 15, and a symptom screen including contact history for children under 10 with HIV. It notes that children accounted for about 12% of TB cases but 16% of deaths in 2019, showing the need for better case detection. It advises placing these tools within national screening and diagnostic algorithms described in the operational handbook.

sections.extract: among children and adolescents 16. Among individuals younger than 15 years who are close contacts of someone with TB, systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted using a symptom screen including any one of cough, fever or poor weight gain; or chest radiography; or both (new recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate to low certainty of evidence for test accuracy). 17. sections.title: Monitoring and evaluation

summary.text: Explains that planning TB screening requires knowing local TB epidemiology, using prevalence surveys or notification data alongside risk factors. It advises monitoring in high-burden settings such as prisons and allows screening to stop when the burden stays low, with surveillance continuing.

sections.extract: 4. Monitoring and evaluation In this section, we consider the monitoring and evaluation required to support the implementation of TB screening programmes. The operational handbook contains more details about the monitoring, surveillance and evaluation of TB screening interventions (7). When considering implementing screening in the general population, it is important to know the epidemiology of TB and the prevalence

sections.title: Indicators

summary.text: Lists indicators for monitoring TB screening in each risk group, from numbers eligible and screened to diagnoses, number needed to screen, initial defaulters and treatment outcomes. It notes the value of disaggregation and the difficulty of estimating eligible populations in community outreach.

sections.extract: Continued monitoring can help programme managers assess the performance of the TB screening components that are within their purview. The following indicators should be considered for each targeted risk group: 1. the number of people eligible for screening; 2. the number of people screened (considering the first screening and second screening separately, if applicable); 3. the proportion of those eligible for

sections.title: Routines for recording and reporting

summary.text: Describes the minimum recording and reporting needed for TB screening indicators, preferably electronic, including logs of people screened and registers of people with presumptive TB. It recommends adding fields to laboratory and treatment registers showing whether patients were found through screening and their risk group.

sections.extract: In order to obtain the required information for the indicators described above, a TB recording and reporting system needs to include a minimal set of data elements. Although paper-based systems have been used to collect such data, it is now becoming increasingly feasible to collect data electronically, and this should be the standard aspired to for monitoring TB screening activities. sections.title: Programmatic evaluations

summary.text: Explains that screening yield may fall over time, so indicators and choices of risk groups, approaches and intervals should be reassessed, with stopping criteria set in advance. It notes that unexpected indicator results may call for special assessments of barriers to screening.

sections.extract: A successful screening programme may lead to a diminishing yield, at least if the risk group is a fixed population. Over time, changes in the background burden of TB, as well as changes in the profile of TB patients in the community (e.g. a trend towards fewer patients with symptomatic TB) can lead to a reduction in the yield from screening, an increase in the NNS, a reduction in cost–effectiveness and a change in

sections.title: Initial calibration for computer-aided detection technologies

summary.text: Advises local calibration of computer-aided detection score thresholds and ongoing monitoring of its performance against human readers and bacteriological results.

sections.extract: technologies When CAD is implemented, local calibration is advised to customize the score thresholds to the requirements of the programme (see the operational handbook for more details about how this can be done) (7). After this initial calibration, ongoing monitoring and analysis of CAD performance should be carried out to assess the correlation with human readers’ interpretations and with bacteriological

sections.extract: 5. Research gaps

sections.title: Screening for TB in targeted populations

summary.text: Identifies research needs on population-wide and targeted TB screening, including trials of effects on individual and population outcomes, implementation choices and long-term cost-effectiveness. It calls for carefully designed observational studies of community screening and more evidence on screening frequency and outcomes for high-risk children.

sections.title: Tools for screening for TB

summary.text: Lists research gaps on screening tools, including CAD performance across patient groups, user acceptability and CAD for children. It also calls for studies of higher C-reactive protein cut-offs in people with HIV and of complete screening and diagnostic algorithms against patient outcomes.

sections.extract: 5.2.1 Computer-aided detection Further evidence is needed about the performance of CAD software stratified according to the characteristics of the individual being evaluated (e.g. by smear status, HIV status, age cohort, history of TB, smoking status, sex) to allow for better setting-specific and patient-specific calibration of CAD programmes. More research on users’ perspectives is needed about CAD technologies in

sections.title: Operational research

summary.text: Suggests operational research topics for TB screening programmes, such as algorithm performance, acceptability, cost-effectiveness and local CAD calibration, and calls for larger randomized trials.

sections.extract: Standard monitoring and evaluation procedures may be complemented by operational research aimed at improving the performance of screening in the local setting as well as research aimed at improving the global evidence base for screening. narratives.en: Fig. 1, a conceptual framework (logic model) for systematic screening for TB, in four columns: Inputs (political and stakeholder engagement, financial resources, human resources, equipment and supplies) feed Activities (screening interventions and activities, including health centre-, community- and household-based activities). These lead to individual-level outcomes (increased TB knowledge, awareness and care-seeking; increased diagnosis and treatment initiation; reduced diagnostic delay; improved treatment outcomes; reduced costs and adverse social consequences) and population-level outcomes (reduced time of infectiousness and prevalence of infectious cases, reduced transmission, and reduced incidence and prevalence of TB).
narratives.ar: الشكل 1، إطار مفاهيمي (نموذج منطقي) للتحري المنهجي عن السل، في أربعة أعمدة: المدخلات (إشراك الجهات السياسية وأصحاب المصلحة، والموارد المالية، والموارد البشرية، والمعدات والإمدادات) تغذي الأنشطة (تدخلات وأنشطة التحري، بما فيها الأنشطة في المراكز الصحية والمجتمعات المحلية والأسر المعيشية). وتؤدي هذه إلى نتائج على مستوى الفرد (زيادة المعرفة بالسل والوعي به والتماس الرعاية؛ وزيادة التشخيص وبدء العلاج؛ وتقليل التأخر في التشخيص؛ وتحسين نتائج العلاج؛ وخفض التكاليف والعواقب الاجتماعية الضارة) ونتائج على مستوى السكان (تقليل مدة العدوى وانتشار الحالات المعدية، وتقليل سريان المرض، وخفض معدل الإصابة بالسل وانتشاره).
narratives.zh: 图1，结核病系统筛查的概念框架（逻辑模型），分为四栏：投入（政治和利益攸关方参与、财政资源、人力资源、设备和用品）支撑活动（筛查干预措施和活动，包括以卫生中心、社区和家庭为基础的活动）。这些活动带来个人层面的结果（结核病知识、意识和求医行为增加；诊断和治疗启动增加；诊断延误减少；治疗结果改善；费用和不良社会后果减少）以及人群层面的结果（传染期和传染性病例患病率降低、传播减少、结核病发病率和患病率降低）。
narratives.es: Figura 1, marco conceptual (modelo lógico) del cribado sistemático de la TB, en cuatro columnas: los insumos (participación política y de las partes interesadas, recursos financieros, recursos humanos, equipos y suministros) alimentan las actividades (intervenciones y actividades de cribado, incluidas actividades en centros de salud, comunidades y hogares). Estas conducen a resultados individuales (mayor conocimiento y concienciación sobre la TB y búsqueda de atención; aumento del diagnóstico y del inicio del tratamiento; menor retraso diagnóstico; mejores resultados del tratamiento; menores costos y consecuencias sociales adversas) y a resultados poblacionales (menor tiempo de infecciosidad y prevalencia de casos infecciosos, menor transmisión y menor incidencia y prevalencia de la TB).
narratives.fr: Figure 1, cadre conceptuel (modèle logique) du dépistage systématique de la tuberculose, en quatre colonnes : les intrants (engagement politique et des parties prenantes, ressources financières, ressources humaines, équipements et fournitures) alimentent les activités (interventions et activités de dépistage, y compris dans les centres de santé, les communautés et les ménages). Celles-ci conduisent à des résultats individuels (meilleure connaissance de la tuberculose, sensibilisation et recours aux soins ; augmentation du diagnostic et de la mise sous traitement ; réduction du retard diagnostique ; amélioration des résultats thérapeutiques ; réduction des coûts et des conséquences sociales néfastes) et à des résultats populationnels (réduction de la durée de contagiosité et de la prévalence des cas contagieux, réduction de la transmission, et baisse de l’incidence et de la prévalence de la tuberculose).
narratives.ru: Рис. 1 — концептуальная основа (логическая модель) систематического скрининга на ТБ в четырёх столбцах: ресурсы (участие политических кругов и заинтересованных сторон, финансовые ресурсы, кадровые ресурсы, оборудование и расходные материалы) обеспечивают мероприятия (скрининговые вмешательства и мероприятия, в том числе в медицинских центрах, общинах и домохозяйствах). Они ведут к результатам на индивидуальном уровне (рост знаний о ТБ, осведомлённости и обращаемости за помощью; увеличение диагностики и начала лечения; сокращение задержки диагностики; улучшение исходов лечения; снижение затрат и неблагоприятных социальных последствий) и на уровне населения (сокращение периода заразности и распространённости заразных случаев, снижение передачи, снижение заболеваемости ТБ и её распространённости).

rows: Screening for TB in targeted populations

Systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted among the general population in areas with an estimated TB prevalence of 0.5% or higher (updated recommendation: conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence).

Systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted among subpopulations with structural risk factors for TB. These include urban poor communities, homeless communities, communities in remote or isolated areas, indigenous populations, migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons and other vulnerable or marginalized groups with limited access to health care (existing recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).
People living with HIV should be systematically screened for TB disease at each visit to a health facility (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

Household contacts and other close contacts of individuals with TB disease should be systematically screened for TB disease (updated recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence).
Systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted in prisons and penitentiary institutions (updated recommendation: strong recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).
Current and former workers in workplaces with silica exposure should be systematically screened for TB disease (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, low certainty of evidence).

In settings where the TB prevalence in the general population is 100/100 000 population or higher, systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted among people with a risk factor for TB who are either seeking health care or who are already in care (existing recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).
People with an untreated fibrotic lesion seen on chest X-ray may be systematically screened for TB disease (existing recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

Among individuals aged 15 years and older in populations in which TB screening is recommended, systematic screening for TB disease may be conducted using a symptom screen, chest X-ray or molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests, alone or in combination (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy).

Among individuals aged 15 years and older in populations in which TB screening is recommended, computer-aided detection software programmes may be used in place of human readers for interpreting digital chest X-rays for screening and triage for TB disease (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence).

Among adults and adolescents living with HIV, systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted using the WHO-recommended four symptom screen and those who report any one of the symptoms of current cough, fever, weight loss or night sweats may have TB and should be evaluated for TB and other diseases (existing recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence).

Among adults and adolescents living with HIV, C-reactive protein using a cut-off of >5mg/L may be used to screen for TB disease (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence for test accuracy).
Among adults and adolescents living with HIV, chest X-ray may be used to screen for TB disease (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy).

Among adults and adolescents living with HIV, molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests may be used to screen for TB disease (new recommendation: conditional recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy).

Adult and adolescent inpatients with HIV in medical wards where the TB prevalence is > 10% should be tested systematically for TB disease with a molecular WHO- recommended rapid diagnostic test (new recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy).

Among individuals younger than 15 years who are close contacts of someone with TB, systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted using a symptom screen including any one of cough, fever or poor weight gain; or chest radiography; or both (new recommendation: strong recommendation, moderate to low certainty of evidence for test accuracy).

Among children younger than 10 years who are living with HIV, systematic screening for TB disease should be conducted using a symptom screen including any one of current cough, fever, poor weight gain or close contact with a TB patient (new recommendation: strong recommendation, low certainty of evidence for test accuracy).
tables.notes: TB: tuberculosis. Column headers are not printed; “No.” and “Recommendation” are supplied. The section header “Screening for TB in targeted populations” is repeated at the top of page 15 and is not repeated here.

narratives.en: The table lists the 17 recommendations of the 2021 WHO guidelines on systematic screening for TB disease, grouped into screening in targeted populations (1–8) and tools for screening (9–17). Each recommendation is followed by its status (new, updated or existing), its strength and the certainty of the evidence.
narratives.ar: يسرد الجدول التوصيات السبع عشرة الواردة في المبادئ التوجيهية للمنظمة لعام 2021 بشأن التحري المنهجي عن مرض السل، مقسمة إلى التحري في الفئات السكانية المستهدفة (1–8) وأدوات التحري (9–17). وتُتبع كل توصية بحالتها (جديدة أو محدَّثة أو قائمة) وقوتها ودرجة اليقين في البيّنات.
narratives.zh: 本表列出了世卫组织2021年结核病系统性筛查指南中的17项建议，分为目标人群筛查（1–8）和筛查工具（9–17）两部分。每项建议后注明其状态（新的、更新的或现有的）、建议强度以及证据确定性。
narratives.es: El cuadro enumera las 17 recomendaciones de las directrices de la OMS de 2021 sobre el cribado sistemático de la enfermedad tuberculosa, agrupadas en cribado en poblaciones destinatarias (1–8) e instrumentos de cribado (9–17). Cada recomendación va seguida de su carácter (nueva, actualizada o existente), su fuerza y la certeza de la evidencia.
narratives.fr: Le tableau présente les 17 recommandations des lignes directrices 2021 de l’OMS sur le dépistage systématique de la tuberculose maladie, regroupées en dépistage dans les populations cibles (1–8) et outils de dépistage (9–17). Chaque recommandation est suivie de son statut (nouvelle, actualisée ou existante), de sa force et du degré de certitude des données.
narratives.ru: В таблице перечислены 17 рекомендаций руководства ВОЗ 2021 г. по систематическому скринингу на туберкулёз, сгруппированных по скринингу в целевых группах населения (1–8) и инструментам скрининга (9–17). После каждой рекомендации указаны её статус (новая, обновлённая или существующая), сила и степень достоверности данных.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Table 2. Risk factors for tuberculosis (TB) to be considered when prioritizing TB screening among people attending for health care

columns.titles: Risk of TB or of poor outcomes

rows: Studies have shown an increased risk of developing TB disease among individuals with fibrotic lesions identified on chest X-ray but who are not diagnosed with TB disease.a

Systematic reviews have found that the risk of TB for patients with DM ranges from 1.5 to 2.0 to 3.1, with a decreasing risk in patients with well-controlled DM. Patients with DM were also at an increased risk of relapse, treatment failure and death.b
Patients with a history of TB are at increased risk of subsequent TB episodes, poor outcomes and developing drug-resistant TB.c
Studies have found hazard ratios for developing TB among individuals with COPD ranging from 2.5 in China to 3.0 in Sweden.d

Systematic reviews have found that people who smoke or who have a history of smoking have an increased risk of TB, with the RR ranging from 1.5 to 2.0 to 3.3; smokers are also at an increased risk of drug-resistant TB and poor outcomes from TB, including relapse and death.e

Systematic reviews have found a 1.35 to 1.9 RR associated with alcohol use and a 3 to 3.33 RR associated with alcohol use disorder, as well as increased risks of treatment failure and development of drug-resistant TB. An exposure–response analysis showed that for every 10–20 g of daily alcohol intake, there was a 12% increase in TB risk.f

People with substance use disorder are at increased risks of treatment failure, development of drug resistance, and mortality from TB due to low adherence and coincident clinical, socioeconomic and structural risk factors.g

A systematic review found that lower BMI is associated with an increased risk of TB, with a reduction in TB incidence of 13.8% (95% confidence interval: 13.4–14.2) per unit increase in BMI within the range 18.5–30 kg/m2. There are multiple pathways by which undernourishment can increase the risk of TB, including cell-mediated immunity and micronutrient deficiency, and other conditions can increase the risk of malnourishment and TB, including mental health and substance use disorders.h

A national registry study found IRRs for TB in pregnant women of 1.4 and of 1.9 for postpartum women compared with non-pregnant women. TB in pregnancy is associated with adverse outcomes and complications during birth. These outcomes include a roughly 2-fold increased risk of premature birth, low birthweight and intrauterine growth retardation, and a 6-fold increased risk of perinatal death.i
Immunocompromising conditions (organ transplant, renal failure, dialysis)

Systematic reviews have found that patients with immunosuppression for reasons other than HIV, including those undergoing organ transplantation or haemodialysis and those with renal failure, have a greatly increased risk of TB: one study found that the incidence of TB is 20–74 times higher in organ transplant patients compared with the general population; one study found that the incidence of TB is 10–25 times higher in dialyzed individuals compared with the general population; and one cohort study found that the incidence of TB is 100 times greater in persons undergoing dialysis compared with general population.j
A systematic review found the IRR of TB disease for health care workers was 2.94 compared with the general population.k

narratives.en: The table lists 11 clinical and other risk factors to consider when prioritizing TB screening among people attending health care, such as fibrotic lesions on chest X-ray, diabetes, previous TB, smoking, alcohol use disorder and pregnancy. For each it summarizes the evidence on the risk of TB or of poor TB outcomes, with references in footnotes.
narratives.ar: يسرد الجدول 11 عامل خطر سريريًا وغيره ينبغي مراعاتها عند إعطاء الأولوية للتحري عن السل بين المترددين على خدمات الرعاية الصحية، مثل الآفات الليفية في صورة الصدر بالأشعة السينية، والسكري، والإصابة السابقة بالسل، والتدخين، واضطراب تعاطي الكحول، والحمل. ويلخص لكل منها البيّنات المتعلقة بخطر الإصابة بالسل أو بسوء نتائجه، مع المراجع في الحواشي.
narratives.zh: 本表列出了在就医人群中确定结核病筛查优先次序时应考虑的11项临床及其他风险因素，如胸部X线纤维化病灶、糖尿病、既往结核病、吸烟、酒精使用障碍和妊娠。对每项因素，表中概述了关于结核病风险或不良结局风险的证据，参考文献见脚注。
narratives.es: El cuadro enumera 11 factores de riesgo clínicos y de otro tipo que deben tenerse en cuenta al priorizar el cribado de la TB entre las personas que acuden a los servicios de salud, como las lesiones fibróticas en la radiografía de tórax, la diabetes, la TB previa, el tabaquismo, el trastorno por consumo de alcohol y el embarazo. Para cada uno resume la evidencia sobre el riesgo de TB o de malos resultados, con las referencias en notas.
narratives.fr: Le tableau présente 11 facteurs de risque, cliniques ou autres, à prendre en compte pour prioriser le dépistage de la tuberculose chez les personnes consultant les services de santé, comme les lésions fibrotiques à la radiographie thoracique, le diabète, des antécédents de tuberculose, le tabagisme, les troubles liés à l’usage de l’alcool et la grossesse. Pour chacun, il résume les données sur le risque de tuberculose ou d’issues défavorables, avec les références en notes.
narratives.ru: В таблице перечислены 11 клинических и иных факторов риска, которые следует учитывать при определении приоритетов скрининга на ТБ среди лиц, обращающихся за медицинской помощью, например фиброзные изменения на рентгенограмме грудной клетки, диабет, ТБ в анамнезе, курение, расстройства, связанные с употреблением алкоголя, и беременность. Для каждого фактора кратко изложены данные о риске ТБ или неблагоприятных исходов со ссылками в сносках.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Table 3. Diagnostic accuracy of symptoms, chest radiography, and molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests for screening for TB disease
rows: Any TB symptom (cough, haemoptysis, fever, night sweats, weight loss)

narratives.en: The table compares the pooled sensitivity and specificity of screening tests for TB disease – cough of different durations, any TB symptom, chest radiography and molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests – against the WHO target product profile, with the number of studies and participants behind each estimate.
narratives.ar: يقارن الجدول الحساسية والنوعية المجمعتين لاختبارات التحري عن مرض السل – السعال بمدد مختلفة، وأي عرض من أعراض السل، والتصوير الشعاعي للصدر، والاختبارات الجزيئية التشخيصية السريعة التي توصي بها المنظمة – مقابل المواصفات المستهدفة للمنتج لدى المنظمة، مع عدد الدراسات والمشاركين الذين يستند إليهم كل تقدير.
narratives.zh: 本表将各项结核病筛查检测——不同持续时间的咳嗽、任何结核病症状、胸部X线摄影以及世卫组织推荐的分子快速诊断检测——的合并敏感度和特异度与世卫组织目标产品特征进行比较，并列出每项估计所依据的研究数和参与者人数。
narratives.es: El cuadro compara la sensibilidad y la especificidad agrupadas de las pruebas de cribado de la enfermedad tuberculosa – tos de distinta duración, cualquier síntoma de TB, radiografía de tórax y pruebas diagnósticas rápidas moleculares recomendadas por la OMS – con el perfil de producto objetivo de la OMS, con el número de estudios y de participantes en que se basa cada estimación.
narratives.fr: Le tableau compare la sensibilité et la spécificité poolées des tests de dépistage de la tuberculose maladie – toux de durées différentes, tout symptôme de tuberculose, radiographie thoracique et tests moléculaires de diagnostic rapide recommandés par l’OMS – au profil de produit cible de l’OMS, avec le nombre d’études et de participants à l’origine de chaque estimation.
narratives.ru: В таблице объединённые чувствительность и специфичность скрининговых тестов на туберкулёз — кашля разной продолжительности, любого симптома ТБ, рентгенографии грудной клетки и рекомендованных ВОЗ молекулярных экспресс-тестов — сопоставлены с целевым профилем продукта ВОЗ, с указанием числа исследований и участников для каждой оценки.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: Table 4. Sensitivity and specificity ranges of computer-aided detection software and human readers interpreting digital chest radiographs for detection of bacteriologically confirmed TB across three software programmes, from three independent evaluations of the software in a range of populations and settings

columns.titles: Type of case and type of reader

tables.notes: CAD: computer-aided detection; CXR: chest X-ray.

narratives.en: The table gives the ranges of sensitivity and specificity of computer-aided detection (CAD) software and of human readers interpreting digital chest X-rays for bacteriologically confirmed TB, separately for the screening and triage use cases, alongside the WHO target product profile.
narratives.ar: يعرض الجدول نطاقات الحساسية والنوعية لبرمجيات الكشف بمساعدة الحاسوب وللقراء البشريين في تفسير صور الصدر الرقمية بالأشعة السينية للكشف عن السل المؤكد جرثوميًا، بشكل منفصل لحالتي استخدام التحري والفرز، إلى جانب المواصفات المستهدفة للمنتج لدى المنظمة.
narratives.zh: 本表列出了计算机辅助检测（CAD）软件和人工阅片者解读数字胸部X线片以检测细菌学确诊结核病的敏感度和特异度范围，按筛查和分诊两种使用情形分别列出，并附世卫组织目标产品特征。
narratives.es: El cuadro presenta los intervalos de sensibilidad y especificidad del software de detección asistida por computadora (DAC) y de los lectores humanos que interpretan radiografías de tórax digitales para la TB confirmada bacteriológicamente, por separado para los usos de cribado y de triaje, junto con el perfil de producto objetivo de la OMS.
narratives.fr: Le tableau présente les fourchettes de sensibilité et de spécificité des logiciels de détection assistée par ordinateur (DAO) et des lecteurs humains interprétant des radiographies thoraciques numériques pour la tuberculose confirmée bactériologiquement, séparément pour les usages de dépistage et de triage, ainsi que le profil de produit cible de l’OMS.
narratives.ru: В таблице приведены диапазоны чувствительности и специфичности программ компьютерной диагностики (CAD) и специалистов, интерпретирующих цифровые рентгенограммы грудной клетки, при выявлении бактериологически подтверждённого ТБ — отдельно для скрининга и сортировки, а также целевой профиль продукта ВОЗ.

tables.label: Table 5
tables.caption: Table 5. Diagnostic accuracy of the WHO-recommended four-symptom screen among different subpopulations of people living with HIV compared with culture as a reference standard
tables.notes: ART: antiretroviral treatment; CI: confidence interval; NA: not applicable.

narratives.ar: يعرض الجدول الحساسية والنوعية (مع فترات ثقة 95%) لـفحص الأعراض الأربعة الذي توصي به المنظمة، مقارنةً بالزرع، في الكشف عن السل لدى المتعايشين مع فيروس العوز المناعي البشري عمومًا وفي فئات فرعية (المرضى الداخليون، والمرضى الخارجيون الذين يتلقون أو لا يتلقون العلاج المضاد للفيروسات القهقرية، ومن لديهم CD4 ≤ 200 خلية/ميكرولتر، والحوامل)، مع عدد الدراسات والمشاركين، مقارنةً بالمواصفات المستهدفة للمنتج لدى المنظمة.
